quotes.text: It wasn't until "Fight for Your Right (to Party)" came out that we started acting like drunken fools. At that point, our image shifted in a different direction, maybe turning off the kids that were strictly into hip-hop. It started off as a goof on that college mentality, but then we ended up personifying it.

We started getting sick of each other and of being on the road, even sick of the band and what it represented, like we were ashamed to be a part of it. We decided to take some time apart from each other.
Leaving Def Jam was kind of a blessing in disguise, because we can make whatever record we want.
The big goal was to make people laugh.
Their process for songwriting involved napkins and shouting
